Ahmed Hossain Khan ------ Appellant
Vs.
Mosammat Hamida Begum Chawdhury and another ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
6. The trial Court decreed the suit on the findings that the plaintiff by the competent  and reliable as well as independent witness proved the fact of payment of TK. 3,50,000/- as earnest money and receipt thereof by the defendant on the date of execution of the agreement dated January 5, 1977 and the said fact of payment of TK.2,50,000/- at the time of execution of the agreement dated January 5, 1977 by the averments made in the agreement (Ext.1) dated January 23, 1977 i.e. the second agreement, that the defendant No. 1 although contended that the plaintiff failed to pay the balance of the consideration money in the light of the agreement dated January 5, 1977 but she failed to prove the said fact by examining independent witness, that the plaintiff has established that he offered balance of the consideration money to the defendant No.1 but she avoided execution and registration of the deed on receiving the balance of the consideration money, that the defendant No.1 in Ext. 1 admitted that she failed to execute and register the sale deed as per stipulation in the agreement dated January 5, 1977, that in Ext. 2 (photocopy of the agreement dated January 5, 1977, the said very document having also been filed by the defendant No.1 was marked as Ext. A) there was stipulation for forfeiture of the earnest money in case of plaintiff's his part and that the agreement would stand cancelled and for return of the part of the earnest money by the defendant No.1, that plaintiff's case of return of TK. 1,20,000/-by the defendant No. 1has been proved by the evidence of P.Ws . 1, 2 and 3 and that defendant's case of refund of Tk. 1,90,000/- to the plaintiff has not been proved by any independent witness or by any documentary evidence, that P.Ws .1, 2 and 3 have proved the execution of the second agreement for sale i.e., agreement for sale dated January 23, 1978, that defendant in support of her case that plaintiff obtained her signature on the agreement dated January 23, 1978 by force did not make any complain at any time prior to filing of a written statement and that while deposing in the Court and that defendant. No.1said case has not been established by examining any other witness, that the defendant No.1 did not lodge any G.D about the fact alleged by her as to taking of her signature by the plaintiff by force with the help of miscreants, that from the defendant No.1 side there was no evidence of independent witness as to taking signature of the defendant No.1 on the second agreement by force by the plaintiff, that signature of the defendant No.1 appearing in the agreement dated January 23, 1978 (Ext.1) appears to have been given "in normal hand" and that signature in the agreement dated January 23, 1978 "was not put under threat or coercion or application of force", that Ext. A claimed to be original of the first agreement appears to be not the one as evidenced by Ext. 2 photocopy of the agreement dated January 5, 1977 since " the style of writing of Ext.2 differ from those of Ext. A" that defendant did not deny her signature appearing in the Ext. 2 nor she claimed that the signature appearing in the Ext.2 is forged and that she had not put any signature in Ext.2 and that defendant " did not take any step for having her signature on the Ext.2 examined by any hand writing expert. Over and above we find that contents of the Ext.2 have been proved and corroborated by the P.Ws. and by the second bainapatra Ext. 1. wherefore Ext. A cannot be presumed to be the first original bainapatra dated 5.1.77", that the suit has been filed "within the statutory period of limitation" and that there was " cause of action for the suit". 

 10. The High Court Division in respect of the contention of the parties relating to the Ext. A which was also marked as Ext. 2 has observed " since the genuineness of Ext. A has not been disputed by the plaintiff- respondent the same, in our view, should be accepted as genuine. Moreover, it appears from the evidence of P.W.1 that the defendant appellant agreed to execute a second agreement of sale and refunded Tk. 1,20,000/- to the plaintiff-respondent from the earnest money she received. This does not happen in normal and usual course of business. It cannot he believed that the Defendant-appellant while agreeing to execute the second sale agreement for selling her property would refund part of the earnest money without adjusting the amount against the total consideration money". 

 11. "From the nature of the evidence and materials on record we are convinced that Ext. 2, said to be the photocopy of the original of the first agreement for sale dated 5.1.77, is a forged one and it is also clear the plaintiff respondent has not been able to prove that the second agreement for sale dated 23.1.78 was executed by the defendant appellant out of her own free will. The possibility that plaintiff- respondent with a view to make illegal gains forced the defendant appellant to put her signature on the second agreement for sale dated 23.1.78 writing her name as Hamida Chowdhury cannot be ruled out in the facts and circumstances of the case. We therefore, find that the plaintiff respondent has not been able to establish that the defendant appellant executed the second agreement of sale (Ext.1) to sell the suit property to the plaintiff respondent out of her own free will. From the evidence on record we are convinced that Ext. A is the first sale agreement between the parties. Ext.2 is a forged document created to pass it off as the first agreement of sale. Since the plaintiff respondent failed to pay the balance consideration money within the stipulated period defendant appellant cancelled the sale agreement (Ext. A) and forfeited part of the earnest money by refunding the balance amount to the plaintiff respondent could not accept this position and as a measure of retaliation he created the second sale agreement (Ext. 1) and obtained the signature of the defendant-appellant thereon by force to grab the suit property". 

 12. It may be mentioned the High Court Division did not accept the contention of the appellant as to hardship, since the defendant appellant could not prove "by evidence that the facts constituting hardship was there from the inception when the agreement of sale was executed" and also observed that" mere fact that there has been rise in the value of the suit property with the lapse of time will not constitute   any hardship" and for that decree for specific performance of contract for sale of land cannot be refused. 

 14. Leave was granted to consider the contentions that in view of the provision of sections 103 and 106 of the Evidence Act defendant No.1 was required to prove the circumstances leading to and the manner in which second agreement dated January 23,1978 was executed as pleaded by the defendant and she having failed to do so by examining corroborative witness and /or proving facts which would support her statements as D.W.1, the High Court Division erred in reversing the decree of the trial Court, that in view of the pleading and filing of the photocopy of the original deed of agreement dated January 5, 1977 and proving the same by the plaintiff appellant as Ext.2, the High Court Division erred in basing its finding on the failure of the plaintiff to challenge Ext. A (agreement dated January 5, 1977 filed by the defendant No.1) by way of putting question to D.W.1 in her cross-examination, that plaintiff proved the case pleaded by him examining one attesting witness (common in Ext. 1 and Ext. A) as well as by the scribe of the second agreement dated January 23, 1978 (Ext. 1) and that the trial Court having decreed the suit upon accepting such prove and upon consideration of the failure of the defendant No.1 to prove her special plea, the High Court Division erred in law in reversing the decree of the trial Court merely on adverse surmise against the plaintiff's case. 

 19. The defendant in support of his case deposed herself alone. In the background of the evidence on record, particularly of the evidence of P.Ws. 1, 3 and 4 the trial Court found the Ext. 1 i.e. agreement; dated January 23, 1978 genuine and disbelieved the case of the defendant since it was not established by the evidence of independent and corroborative witness, that the signature in Ext. 1 was obtained by force by the plaintiff and thereupon decreed the suit. 

 20. The High Court Division in the absence of any corroborative evidence from the side of the defendant held that the signature of the defendant was obtained by force and that she did not execute the Ext. 1 "out of her own free will". The High Court Division surmised that as the defendant No.1 forfeited the part of the earnest money the said fact was not appreciated by the plaintiff and thereupon " as a measure of retaliation he created the second sale agreement ( Ext.1) and obtained the signature of the defendant appellant thereon by force to grab the suit property". It may be mentioned the trial Court has noticed the fact that prior to the filing of the written statement and deposing in Court the defendant No.1 did not complain about the Ext. 1 in any manner. The High Court Division lost sight of the tact, that defendant's contention that her signature in Ext. 1 was obtained by force, as alleged by her, was not established by the evidence of any independent witness corroborating the defendant No.1 as to the fact as alleged by her as to obtaining her signature in Ext. 1 by force. In that state of the matter we are of the view High Court Division was in serious error in holding that the Ext.1 is not a genuine one since signature of the defendant No.1 thereon was obtained by force. The plaintiff in support of his case that defendant No.1 executed the Ext.1 i.e. agreement dated January 23, 1978 has deposed himself and he has been corroborated by the P.Ws.3 and 4, attesting witness and the scribe respectively. The High Court Division did not assign any reason for discarding their evidence or in other words leaving the evidence of those witnesses out of consideration. The High Court Division in disregard of the evidence of Pws.1, 3 and 4 particularly and also the evidence of P.W. 2 was in serious error in holding that signature of the defendant No.1 was obtained in Ext.1 by force. It is seen the High Court Division has not considered the evidence of PWs. particularly P.Ws. 1, 3 and 4 as well as of P.W.2 on no legally sustainable reason. It is seen from the judgment of the trial Court that defendant No. 1 did not deny her signature in Ext.2 i.e. photocopy of the agreement dated January 5, 1977. In that state of the matter plaintiff was not required to establish the genuineness of the Exc. 2. In our view in the background the facts and circumstances of the case as well as upon due scrutiny of the document i.e.  Ext. A, the finding made by the trial Court as to Ext. A was quite correct. The High Court Division in disregard of the evidence on record was in error in disturbing the finding of the trial Court as to Ext. A while reversing the decree passed by the trial Court. It was the plea of the defendant No. 1 that her signature in Ext.1 was obtained by force by the plaintiff with the help of miscreants. In the background of the aforesaid case of the defendant it was incumbent upon her to establish the said fact by corroborative witness, but she having had failed to do so the High Court Division was in error in holing that signature of the defendant No.1 was obtained in Ext.1 by force and thereupon observing that the said agreement was brought into existence by the plaintiff as a measure of retaliation and to grab the property of the defendant No.1. 

 21. The law is now settled that one who alleges certain fact and urges upon the Court to accept the same for giving verdict in one's favour, one is to establish the said fact by competent witness and that at sometimes by corroborative evidence. In the instant case defendant No.1 failed to prove her case of obtaining her signature in Ext.1 forcibly by the plaintiff. In the facts and circumstances of the case when the genuineness of the Ext. 1 is not disproved by the defendant No.1 in our view the Ext. 2 and the Ext. A were not so much so material and also had no bearing on the point involved in the suit and as such the High Court Division was in error in placing importance thereon and thereupon dis believing the case of the plaintiff based on the Ext.1 when the genuineness thereof of was established by the competent witnesses and that defendant No.1 failed to dislodged the genuineness thereof by examining reliable and competent witness.
